rules: Access, closure, route, ownership, and regulation claims are recorded separately from biological opportunity.
A broad lake, county, port, harbor, or fishing-mode source is never presented as an exact-structure catch rate.
Secondary and specialist reports can corroborate timing or a rare occurrence, but do not override primary creel evidence.

sources.title: Fishing Areas
sources.geography: Chicago lakefront, named harbors, and north side of Navy Pier
sources.claim: Year-round shore fishing, hours, winter harbor pass, north-side-only Navy Pier access, and the agency's broad month-by-month species calendar.
sources.use: Primary access and broad seasonal context; not a Montrose or Navy Pier catch-rate source.
sources.limitation: The biological calendar is citywide and combines multiple structures. The page uses 'silver bass' in a way that is not safe evidence for white bass.

sources.title: Family Fishing at Montrose Harbor
sources.geography: Montrose Harbor fishing pier west of the boat launch
sources.claim: Confirms the named Montrose fishing-pier location.
sources.use: Primary boundary and access identity.
sources.limitation: An event page is not a complete access policy or biological survey.

sources.title: Survey of Sport Fishing in the Illinois Portion of Lake Michigan, 2023
sources.geography: Illinois Lake Michigan; tables include Montrose and a winter pedestrian survey including Navy Pier
sources.mode: pedestrian creel interview and effort estimate
sources.claim: Documents strong spring coho and winter yellow-perch shore fisheries; exact Montrose table rows include salmon and perch observations.
sources.use: Primary quantitative evidence with table-level geography retained.
sources.limitation: Some headline totals pool sites; winter sampling emphasizes perch and does not fully quantify every trout species.

sources.title: Survey of Sport Fishing in the Illinois Portion of Lake Michigan, 2024
sources.geography: Illinois Lake Michigan; Montrose pedestrian rows
sources.mode: pedestrian creel interview and effort estimate
sources.claim: Montrose rows record coho and brown trout in spring, heavy yellow-perch catch in June, and Chinook/coho in September.
sources.use: Primary exact-site seasonal evidence for April through September.
sources.limitation: The Montrose table does not cover winter; a zero in this seasonal table cannot establish year-round absence.

sources.title: Lake Michigan fishing overview
sources.geography: Illinois Lake Michigan
sources.claim: Describes the managed fishery, shore opportunity, habitat, and stocked salmonids.
sources.use: Primary regional corroboration and management context.
sources.limitation: Cannot be transferred directly to either covered Chicago structure.

sources.title: Montrose Harbor fishing reports 270, 271, 277, 283, and 285
sources.geography: Montrose Horseshoe, harbor mouth, walls, powerlines, and nearby lakefront
sources.mode: shore and harbor angling; boat reports separated where stated
sources.claim: Recurring exact-area reports identify coho, Chinook, steelhead, brown trout, perch, smallmouth bass, freshwater drum, and northern pike across spring through early fall.
sources.use: Current specialist corroboration for named Montrose subareas and timing.
sources.limitation: Qualitative reports are selective and supply no standardized effort denominator; each linked report must be checked before using a narrower claim.

sources.title: Lake trout trending upward in winter from the Chicago lakefront
sources.geography: Chicago lakefront, including Navy Pier
sources.claim: Reports a stronger 2022-23 winter lake-trout bite and cites an INHS biologist on the increase, with a longer record of incidental Navy Pier catches.
sources.use: Exact seasonal lead supporting lake trout as a high-priority Pass 2 candidate.
sources.limitation: News and expert observations do not provide standardized effort or a multi-year site table.

sources.title: Chicago Report, March 2025 digital edition
sources.geography: Chicago winter lakefront and named harbors
sources.mode: shore, pier, and winter harbor dock
sources.claim: Reports winter perch and lake-trout opportunity before severe cold and explains the harbor winter-pass context.
sources.use: Specialist corroboration for a non-fall lake-trout window.
sources.limitation: Qualitative and not structure-level effort sampling.

sources.title: Top 10 fishing spots in the Chicago area
sources.geography: Montrose Harbor
sources.claim: Documents a single angler catching the Illinois-record burbot and lake whitefish at Montrose on 2017-03-22.
sources.use: Historical occurrence lead only.
sources.limitation: One exceptional day cannot establish a recurring or forecastable fishery.

sources.title: Fishing Pass Application
sources.geography: Navy Pier Marina
sources.claim: Documents the current pass-controlled fishing program at Navy Pier Marina.
sources.use: Primary operator access source, read with Chicago Park District's north-side rule.
sources.limitation: Seasonal details and construction routing may change; confirm live before release.

sources.title: 2026 Illinois Fishing Information
sources.geography: Illinois Lake Michigan and statewide
sources.claim: Current seasons, size and possession limits, including the Lake Michigan yellow-perch closure and smelt season.
sources.use: Primary regulation gate only.
sources.limitation: A legal season does not prove biological opportunity; local Chicago rules can be narrower.

sources.title: Washington Park
sources.geography: Washington Park, Michigan City
sources.mode: public park and East Pier approach
sources.claim: Confirms the city park, lakefront address, and walk-out pier setting.
sources.use: Primary access and boundary source.
sources.limitation: Parking, beach fees, weather closures, and posted pier restrictions require live confirmation.

sources.title: Lake Michigan Fishing
sources.geography: Indiana Lake Michigan; names Michigan City pier, basin, and inner harbor
sources.mode: shore, pier, tributary, and boat modes separated in text
sources.claim: Names public access and seasonal shore fisheries for coho, fall salmon, Skamania steelhead, perch, bass, and sunfish.
sources.use: Primary current biological and access framework.
sources.limitation: Some species statements are regional; Trail Creek and the NIPSCO discharge are separate locations and cannot be transferred to East Pier.

sources.title: Fishing Lake Michigan Shoreline and Tributaries
sources.geography: Indiana Lake Michigan shore sites, including Washington Park marina and Michigan City pier
sources.claim: Separates pier timing for coho, Chinook, summer and winter steelhead, perch, bass, and sunfish; characterizes lake trout as primarily a boat opportunity.
sources.use: Primary mode-specific season guide and negative mode constraint.
sources.limitation: Older qualitative guide without standardized local effort; current regulations prevail.

sources.title: Spring Coho Shore Fishing 101
sources.geography: Washington Park pier and DNR/Coast Guard inner harbor
sources.claim: Names the exact access points, January through mid-April coho window, March consistency, and possible brown-trout or whitefish bycatch on bottom rigs.
sources.use: Primary exact-site timing and lake-whitefish research lead.
sources.limitation: Technique guide, not a creel estimate; whitefish is presented as a possibility rather than measured recurrence.

sources.title: Indiana Fishing Reports
sources.geography: Michigan City shore and surrounding Indiana waters
sources.mode: shore, tributary, and boat reports distinguished
sources.claim: Reports a few coho and Chinook from Michigan City shore in mid-September 2026.
sources.use: Current primary corroboration for fall salmon shore presence.
sources.limitation: A weekly qualitative report does not isolate East Pier effort or magnitude.

sources.title: 2026-27 Indiana Fishing Guide and Regulations
sources.geography: Indiana
sources.claim: Current Lake Michigan and statewide fishing regulations.
sources.use: Primary regulation gate only.
sources.limitation: Regulations do not establish catch opportunity and posted local closures can supersede access assumptions.

sources.title: Creel Sportfishing Estimates dashboard export
sources.geography: Port labels MUSKEGON, WHITEHALL-MONTAGUE, and ALPENA
sources.claim: Provides species, month, catch, harvest, and angler-hour estimates for surveyed strata, including explicit zeros.
sources.use: Primary quantitative occurrence and recurrence evidence for the three Michigan ports; raw export is preserved in this package.
sources.limitation: Port and mode aggregates can combine more than one structure or side; missing strata differ from zeros; estimates have uncertainty; winter is incompletely sampled; the public export stops at 2022.

sources.title: Creel Fishing Reports and Creel Survey
sources.geography: Michigan
sources.claim: Explains interview collection of location, fishing mode, target, duration, and catch.
sources.use: Primary methods documentation for interpreting the dashboard extract.
sources.limitation: Does not itself provide site-specific results.

sources.title: 2025 Michigan Great Lakes Recreational Fisheries: Creel Surveys, Charter Reporting, and Historical Trends, Fisheries Report 49
sources.geography: Michigan Great Lakes
sources.mode: lakewide and basinwide modes, including pier/dock
sources.claim: Current creel methods and 2025 Great Lakes summaries; supplement includes Lake Michigan and Lake Huron pier/dock tables.
sources.use: Current mode-level corroboration and methods context.
sources.limitation: The 2025 tables aggregate whole lakes and cannot update any of the three named ports directly.

sources.title: Supplemental material for Fisheries Report 49: 2025 Michigan Great Lakes Recreational Fisheries
sources.geography: Michigan Great Lakes; whole-lake tables
sources.mode: separate boat, ice, pier/dock, shore, and total tables
sources.claim: Provides 2025 Lake Michigan and Lake Huron Pier/Dock estimates by month and species.
sources.use: Current mode-level corroboration only; reviewed workbook SHA-256 is 0e75be0192503121bbae719e982b1a15fd17d6e5319cda4bc8a6816800c07376.
sources.limitation: The Pier/Dock worksheets contain no port or structure field, so they cannot update Muskegon, Whitehall-Montague, or Alpena directly.

sources.title: Better Fishing Waters
sources.geography: Named Michigan waters including Muskegon/White Lake pier and channel waters and Thunder Bay/Alpena Harbor
sources.mode: pier, channel, and harbor where named
sources.claim: Names Chinook, lake whitefish, steelhead, and perch for Muskegon and White Lake pier/channel waters; names a broad salmonid, coolwater, and warmwater set for Thunder Bay/Alpena Harbor.
sources.use: Primary named-water candidate evidence.
sources.limitation: Qualitative list without effort, timing, or exact breakwall-side allocation.

sources.title: Central Lake Michigan Management Unit
sources.geography: Muskegon channel, north platforms, south pier, and separately described Muskegon River
sources.claim: Provides coordinates, routes, and a channel species list including salmon, steelhead, brown trout, whitefish, perch, channel catfish, walleye, drum, and bass.
sources.use: Primary exact-area access and biological source.
sources.limitation: The channel list is qualitative and may pool walls, platforms, and both sides; the upstream river paragraph is excluded.

sources.title: Muskegon State Park
sources.geography: North Muskegon channel walkway and fishing decks
sources.claim: Identifies the north channel walkway and two fishing decks and carries a construction closure extending through August 2026 with reopening anticipated as early as fall.
sources.use: Primary closure gate; requires live verification because the anticipated reopening window has arrived.
sources.limitation: An anticipated reopening is not confirmation that the path is open on the report date.

sources.title: Muskegon Lake Status of the Fishery Resource Report 0448
sources.geography: Muskegon Lake and channel/pierhead habitat
sources.claim: Specifically notes smallmouth bass in channel and pierhead areas and documents the broader fish community.
sources.use: Primary habitat corroboration, especially for channel smallmouth.
sources.limitation: Fishery assessment presence is not a pier angler catch rate.

sources.publisher: White Lake Area Chamber and Convention & Visitors Bureau
sources.title: Medbery Park
sources.geography: Medbery Park on the north side of the White Lake outlet channel, White River Township
sources.claim: Lists 7340 Life Guard Road, fishing along the channel, accessible facilities, 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. hours, and City of Montague ownership.
sources.use: Local operator boundary, ownership, and hours source.
sources.limitation: The report label is Whitehall, but the covered public site is outside Whitehall city limits and is owned by Montague.

sources.title: White Lake Status of the Fishery Resource Report
sources.geography: White Lake and its Lake Michigan connection
sources.claim: Documents White Lake fish community and seasonal connection to Lake Michigan.
sources.use: Primary system context for interpreting port creel evidence.
sources.limitation: Does not isolate Medbery Park or channel-edge angling.

sources.publisher: Thunder Bay Island Lighthouse Preservation Society
sources.title: Visit Alpena Light
sources.geography: Municipal breakwall adjacent to Bay View Park, Alpena
sources.claim: Provides approach, parking context, and exact lighthouse coordinates; distinguishes public breakwall access from the closed tower.
sources.use: Local exact-structure boundary and route source.
sources.limitation: Non-government operator page; posted weather or security closures still require live confirmation.

sources.title: Planning Commission packet, 2024-01-09
sources.geography: Alpena breakwall and Bay View Park
sources.claim: Documents the long breakwall walkway, railing, lighting, fishing platform, and benches.
sources.use: Primary physical-boundary and public-use corroboration.
sources.limitation: Planning records do not establish real-time opening status or fish opportunity.

sources.title: Planning Commission packet containing harbor and marina fishing ordinance
sources.geography: Alpena harbor and marina
sources.claim: Permits fishing in harbor/marina areas subject to posted rules, security, and privacy constraints.
sources.use: Primary municipal access-rule context.
sources.limitation: Posted signs and temporary closures control on-site behavior.

sources.title: 2026 Michigan Fishing Regulations
sources.geography: Michigan
sources.claim: Current statewide and Great Lakes fishing regulations, including species limits and special port rules.
sources.use: Primary regulation gate only.
sources.limitation: A regulation does not prove opportunity and local closures can change access.

sources.title: Single-pointed hook regulations Nov. 1-30
sources.geography: Named Michigan ports including Muskegon and Whitehall-Montague
sources.claim: Explains November single-point-hook restrictions and their whitefish-protection purpose in named port waters.
